independent_reference.source: Onsager, L. (1944), Crystal statistics. I. A two-dimensional model with an order-disorder transition, Phys. Rev. 65, 117, section V. The exact 2D square-lattice critical temperature is T_c = 2 J / ln(1 + sqrt(2)) = 2.269185314213022 for J = 1 (k_B = 1).

Kramers, H. A. & Wannier, G. H. (1941), Statistics of the two-dimensional ferromagnet. Part I, Phys. Rev. 60, 252. The self-dual point sinh(2 beta_c J) = 1 gives beta_c = (1/2) asinh(1) = (1/2) ln(1 + sqrt(2)), hence T_c = 1/beta_c = 2/ln(1+sqrt(2)) = 2.269185314213022. Hand-derivation: tools/testkit/golden/derivations/ising-onsager.md section 2.

Landau, D. P. & Binder, K. (2014), A Guide to Monte Carlo Simulations in Statistical Physics, 4th ed., Cambridge University Press, chapter 4 (2D Ising critical temperature T_c/J = 2.26919...). Cite-by-edition; the five-figure textbook value agrees with the Onsager closed form within the relative tolerance 1e-3 (|2.26919 - 2.269185314| = 4.7e-6).
